## SPEC DEFECT — the phase-close certificate cannot carry a relative decay test

| asset | mean PHASE-CLOSE cert at tau=0 | mean PEAK-EXIT cert at tau=0 | degenerate flag | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SI | $-15.03 | $967.05 | 1.0 | `artifacts/cache/port/m1/decay/decay_cells.tsv:1925` |
| HG | $-28.36 | $730.61 | 1.0 | `artifacts/cache/port/m1/decay/decay_cells.tsv:3973` |
| NKD | $-44.98 | $833.78 | 1.0 | `artifacts/cache/port/m1/decay/decay_cells.tsv:6021` |

§2 says the certificate is the "phase-close exit variant". Pooled over every
confirmation, that certificate has a mean of **minus a few tens of dollars** —
the walled phase-close value of an unselected candidate is a near-zero,
sign-indefinite quantity. "Mean value decay < 1.5% vs tau=0" against a negative
denominator is not a weak test, it is an inverted one: a value moving from
-$15.03 to -$13.52 (an IMPROVEMENT) reads as "10% decay".

Resolution applied (declared before the numbers were read, on two criteria that
have nothing to do with which tau they select): the pin population must be
UNSELECTED, and the tau=0 denominator must not be degenerate. Only the
peak-exit certificate over all confirmations satisfies both, and its scale
($730-$967) is the scale D-033 quotes. Every other reading §2's wording admits
is still evaluated and emitted in the pin-rule TSV, including the $1k-class
population, which is SELECTION-BIASED by construction (it conditions on the
tau=0 outcome, so regression to the mean can only make later entries look
worse) and is the one reading that pins tau* at the 30s floor.

The absolute numbers make the ambiguity moot in practice: over 120 seconds the
phase-close mean MOVES UP by $0.51-$2.12 per candidate and the peak-exit mean
moves by -$2.04 to +$0.32 on a $730-$967 base. There is no decay to measure at
this granularity.

Per-tau evidence for every reading: `artifacts/cache/port/m1/decay/decay_pin_rule.tsv`.

The §2 universe is re-derived from the sessions with m0's own `zigzag_scan`, thresholds and dedup; at tau=60 it reproduces the frozen m0 roster and its §8 phase-close certificates exactly (579,040 candidates, zero mismatches). Getting there required quantising the excursion prefix maxima to float32: the m0 skeleton stores them that way, excursions live on a $12.50 grid and the wall is $900, so a float64 recomputation disagrees with m0 on exact-wall ties (954/189,821 SI candidates before the fix).
